Leeds Recycling Firm Wins £3m Council Contract

LEEDS, UK — 4 February 2026 — Kirkgate Recovery has won a five-year, £3m contract to process household recycling for Leeds City Council, replacing a provider that collapsed in November.

“The council needed someone operational within six weeks, and we were the only bidder who could say yes honestly,” said Dev Mistry, Kirkgate’s operations director. “We’d already commissioned the second sorting line in October, so the capacity was sitting there.

“What we hadn’t planned for was hiring 22 people in a fortnight. That’s the part that kept me up at night, and it’s the part I’m proudest of.”

The contract covers about 340,000 households and starts on 1 March. Kirkgate’s existing plant on Gelderd Road will handle the volume after a £400,000 upgrade completed last month.

Kirkgate took over the round on an emergency six-week interim arrangement in December after the previous contractor, Northbridge Waste, entered administration with 11 days’ notice. Recycling rates across the city held at 43% through the handover, against a 39% figure for the same period a year earlier.

The firm has taken on 22 permanent staff, 14 of them former Northbridge employees, and has committed to a further £250,000 of plant investment in the second year of the contract.

Councillor Ruth Ellery, executive member for environment, said the authority “could not have asked for a smoother handover in the circumstances”.

About Kirkgate Recovery
Kirkgate Recovery is a materials recovery business founded in Leeds in 2011. It processes around 90,000 tonnes of recyclate a year for local authority and commercial customers across Yorkshire, and employs 140 people.
